Subject: Quick pilot idea — Datadog + Grafana OTLP bridge for Acme

Irene / Ben —

Thanks again for the discussion last week. Acme Retail (Ethan Brooks, cc'd) is piloting a multi-tool telemetry stack and has a hard requirement: they want a single OTLP path that can feed both Datadog and Grafana Cloud without duplicating instrumentation.

Datadog's field team and Grafana partners think a short technical pilot (3 weeks) that validates an OTLP bridge + routing rules would unblock a much larger procurement discussion. The ask: can Redwood run an integration pilot that demonstrates prefix-based routing, tag preservation, and a performance profile for 1k eps?

Key constraints from Acme:
- No agent changes on their side (we must reuse existing SDKs)
- Retention and export controls per workload (security/compliance)
- Cost target: keep added per-token/ingest cost under their current threshold

Would Redwood be able to scope a minimal SOW to prove feasibility? Ben / Laura — looping you for feasibility and any obvious blockers.

Best,
Aidan
Datadog — Strategic Partnerships

Thanks Aidan — this is doable and thanks for looping Marta.

High-level proposal from Redwood:
1) Pilot scope (3 weeks):
   - Validate a bridge that accepts OTLP/gRPC from Acme SDKs and fans out to both Datadog and Grafana Cloud.
   - Verify tag/trace-context fidelity and prefix-based routing rules.
   - Measure latency and cost at 1k events/sec sustained and under a 5s P95 latency SLO.
2) Deliverables:
   - Working deployment in Redwood sandbox + ingestion diagrams
   - Test harness and sample scripts for synthetic load
   - Short SOW describing data controls and retention options
3) Roles: Redwood (infra + integration), Datadog (ingest mapping guidance), Grafana (cloud routing profile), Acme (test data + acceptance criteria)

Ben and Laura — can your teams draft a minimal SOW and an architecture diagram? I'm attaching a rough draft of the SOW and an architecture sketch for quick feedback.

Ethan — can you confirm a non-prod endpoint and a test key we can use? Also confirm whether the security team needs an NDA addendum for the pilot export flows.

I'll propose a short kickoff next Wednesday for 30 minutes if folks are available.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
T: 555-0102

Irene — quick feasibility notes from infra:

- Implementation approach: we can implement a lightweight fanout proxy in our sandbox that accepts OTLP/gRPC, applies routing rules, and forwards to vendor endpoints. We'll support both full payload forward and sample-only paths.
- Data controls: we have hooks for redaction and field filtering; will need to confirm which fields Acme considers PII.
- Performance: 1k eps is small; the work here is verifying connector mappings and ensuring we don't increase tail latency. We'll instrument KV cache and batching thresholds for the pilot.

I'll prepare an architecture slide plus a test plan and add a small section on cost assumptions (eg. expected token/ingest equivalence for billing). Laura, can you scope a short runbook for acceptance tests?

Ben
Senior Integration Engineer, Redwood
